_about: Common mistakes per concept. Each wrong option of a question names one of these, so the same mistake made on different questions is recognised as a repeat. Safe to edit labels; changing an id breaks the link to questions already using it.

electric-charge.label: Thinks rubbing creates charge, rather than moving electrons from one body to the other
Thinks positive charges (protons) move when a body is charged
Thinks charging by induction needs contact, or that the inducing body loses charge
Thinks charge spreads over an insulator the way it does over a conductor

charge-quantisation.label: Thinks a body can carry any amount of charge, including a fraction of e
Expects quantisation to be noticeable in everyday, large-scale charges
Gets the sign wrong: losing electrons leaves a body positive

charge-conservation.label: Thinks charge is destroyed when opposite charges neutralise or a body is earthed
Confuses conservation of total charge with each body staying neutral
Thinks conservation means charged particles can never be created or destroyed

coulombs-law.label: Thinks the larger charge pulls harder on the smaller one (forgets Newton's third law)
Forgets that a medium weakens the force by the factor K
Confuses the direction in the vector form: signs of the charges vs the unit vector

superposition-principle.label: Adds the sizes of forces instead of adding them as vectors
Thinks a third charge changes the force between the other two
Assumes forces cancel by symmetry when the arrangement is not actually symmetric

electric-field.label: Thinks the field at a point depends on the test charge placed there
Thinks a negative charge is pushed along the field direction
Thinks there is no field at a point unless a charge is placed there
Uses 1/r instead of 1/r² for the field of a point charge

field-lines.label: Treats field lines as the paths charges actually follow
Misreads how closely spaced the lines are (closer means a stronger field)
Thinks electrostatic field lines form closed loops

electric-dipole.label: Takes the dipole moment as pointing from + to − (it points from − to +)
Uses 1/r² instead of 1/r³ for the field far from a dipole
Mixes up the axial and equatorial fields (the factor of 2, or the direction)

dipole-in-field.label: Thinks a dipole in a uniform field feels a net force
Uses cos θ instead of sin θ for the torque
Mixes up stable equilibrium (p along E) and unstable (p opposite E)

electric-flux.label: Thinks flux depends only on area, ignoring the angle
Measures the angle from the surface instead of from its normal
Ignores sign: treats inward and outward flux as both positive

gauss-law.label: Thinks charges outside the surface change the net flux
Thinks the E in Gauss's law comes only from the charges inside
Thinks the net flux depends on the size or shape of the surface
Thinks zero net flux means zero field everywhere on the surface

gauss-applications.label: Thinks the field inside a charged spherical shell is not zero
Uses 1/r² instead of 1/r for a long straight line of charge
Thinks the field of an infinite flat sheet weakens with distance
Picks a Gaussian surface without the symmetry needed to take E out of the integral

electrostatic-potential.label: Thinks potential has a direction, like a vector
Thinks zero potential at a point means zero field there, or the reverse
Mixes up potential (energy per unit charge) with potential energy
Gets the sign of the work wrong when a charge moves to a higher potential

potential-point-charge.label: Ignores the sign of the charge when adding potentials
Adds potentials as vectors instead of as plain numbers

equipotential-surfaces.label: Thinks work is needed to move a charge along an equipotential surface
Thinks the field can point along an equipotential surface (it is always perpendicular)
Thinks equipotentials around a point charge are evenly spaced for equal steps of V

potential-energy-charges.label: Counts pairs twice, or misses pairs, when adding up a system of charges
Thinks two like charges have negative potential energy
Thinks the energy belongs to one charge rather than to the whole arrangement
Thinks the energy depends on the order the charges were brought in

conductors-electrostatics.label: Thinks the field inside a charged conductor is not zero
Thinks extra charge spreads through a conductor's volume instead of sitting on its surface
Thinks the field just outside a conductor can be at an angle to the surface
Thinks charge spreads evenly over an irregular conductor (it gathers at sharp points)

dielectrics-polarisation.label: Thinks a dielectric has free charges that move as in a conductor
Thinks a dielectric cancels the field inside completely, like a conductor
Gets the effect of K backwards: thinks a dielectric strengthens the field inside

capacitance.label: Thinks capacitance depends on the charge stored or the voltage applied
Thinks a charged capacitor's net charge is Q (it is +Q and −Q, so zero)
Reads C = Q/V as more charge gives more capacitance

parallel-plate-capacitor.label: Thinks capacitance increases with plate separation
Forgets the factor K, or puts it in the wrong place, when a dielectric fills the gap
Thinks a slab partly filling the gap leaves C unchanged

capacitor-combinations.label: Swaps the rules: adds capacitances in series, like resistors
Thinks capacitors in series share the same voltage (they carry the same charge)
Thinks capacitors in parallel carry the same charge (they share the same voltage)

energy-in-capacitor.label: Thinks the energy is stored in the plates rather than in the field between them
Mixes up what stays fixed when a dielectric goes in: battery connected (V fixed) or disconnected (Q fixed)

electric-current.label: Takes the current direction as the direction electrons move
Thinks current gets used up as it passes through a bulb or resistor

drift-velocity.label: Thinks electrons drift at nearly the speed of light (confusing it with how fast the signal travels)
Confuses drift velocity with the electrons' fast random thermal motion
Thinks electrons drift along the field (they drift against it)
Gets how drift speed changes with wire thickness, for the same current, wrong

ohms-law.label: Thinks Ohm's law holds for every material and device
Reads R = V/I as resistance depends on V or I

resistivity.label: Confuses resistance (depends on shape) with resistivity (a property of the material)
Thinks stretching a wire changes its resistivity
Gets the change in resistance wrong when a wire is stretched (n times longer gives n² times the resistance)
Thinks resistivity is a force pushing against the field, rather than a measure of how freely charges move

temperature-resistivity.label: Thinks every material's resistivity rises with temperature (a semiconductor's falls)
Thinks alloys like manganin change strongly with temperature (they barely change)
Thinks resistance rises because the wire expands, not because of more collisions

electrical-energy-power.label: Uses V²/R or I²R without checking which quantity is shared (series or parallel)
Thinks a higher-wattage bulb has a higher resistance
Thinks energy turns into heat even where charges move without colliding

resistor-combinations.label: Swaps the series and parallel rules
Thinks resistors in parallel carry the same current
Thinks a parallel combination can be larger than its smallest resistor
Treats resistors as series or parallel when they are neither (that needs Kirchhoff's rules)

emf-internal-resistance.label: Thinks terminal voltage always equals the emf
Gets the sign wrong while charging: V = ε + Ir versus ε − Ir
Thinks the most current flows when the external resistance is largest

kirchhoffs-rules.label: Uses inconsistent signs going around a loop
Treats the loop rule as comparing emfs with resistances instead of adding up voltage drops
Does not see that the junction rule is conservation of charge
Thinks a negative current in the answer means a mistake (it means the guessed direction was backwards)

wheatstone-bridge.label: Pairs the resistors wrongly in the balance condition (P/Q = R/S)
Thinks current flows through the galvanometer at balance
Thinks balance depends on the battery's emf or the galvanometer's resistance

magnetic-force.label: Thinks a magnetic field pushes on a charge at rest
Thinks the magnetic force points along the field or along the velocity
Thinks the magnetic force does work and changes the speed
Forgets to reverse the direction for a negative charge

lorentz-force.label: Adds the electric and magnetic forces as sizes instead of as vectors
Thinks the magnetic part still acts when v is parallel to B
Gets the velocity-selector condition wrong (it is v = E/B)

motion-in-magnetic-field.label: Puts the mass in the wrong place in r = mv/qB
Thinks the time for one circle depends on the speed (it does not)
Thinks a charge moving at an angle to B goes in a circle (it is a helix)
Thinks the charge speeds up as it circles

cyclotron.label: Thinks the magnetic field speeds the particle up (the electric field between the dees does)
Thinks the oscillator's frequency must change as the particle speeds up (it stays constant)
Thinks the final energy depends on the voltage between the dees, rather than on the radius and B

biot-savart-law.label: Gets the direction of dB wrong (it is perpendicular to both dl and r)
Thinks a point straight along the line of the current element feels a field (it is zero there)

field-circular-loop.label: Mixes up the field at the centre (μ₀I/2R) with the formula for points on the axis
Gets the direction of the field on the axis wrong
Thinks the components along the axis cancel (it is the sideways ones that cancel)

amperes-circuital-law.label: Thinks currents outside the loop change the line integral
Thinks B on the loop comes only from the currents inside it
Applies it without the symmetry needed to take B out of the integral

solenoid-toroid.label: Uses the total number of turns N instead of turns per unit length n
Thinks the field inside a long solenoid depends on its radius or position
Thinks there is a field outside an ideal toroid, or in its open middle

force-between-currents.label: Gets it backwards: thinks parallel currents repel and opposite currents attract
Thinks the wire with more current feels the bigger force
Uses 1/r² instead of 1/r for the force per unit length

torque-current-loop.label: Thinks a current loop in a uniform field feels a net force
Measures the angle from the coil's plane instead of from its normal
Thinks the torque is largest when the coil's plane is perpendicular to B

moving-coil-galvanometer.label: Thinks the radial field is there to make the field stronger (it keeps the torque the same at every angle, so the scale is even)
Swaps the conversions: an ammeter needs a small resistor in parallel (shunt), a voltmeter a large one in series
Thinks raising current sensitivity always raises voltage sensitivity too
Confuses field perpendicular to the coil's plane with field perpendicular to the wires
